messages.author: 85679393b8bc3d9b
messages.subject: warpRefMesh question
parts:
Hi everyone,

Just want to make sure I am doing an analysis in geomorph correctly. My goal is to show the shape changes at the extremes (min and max) of PC axes 1-4. Before doing so and outside geomorph, I identified the specimens at the extreme of each PC of interest (e.g. point.pc1.min <- df_out[df_out$PC1 == min(df_out$PC1),] & point.pc1.min <- df_out[df_out$PC1 == max(df_out$PC1),]). Next, I read in the meshes associated with those extremes accordingly using the read.ply function. I then used the meanshape function to find the meanshape across all landmarks (e.g. mshape <- mshape(land) and finally used warpRefMesh to plot the shape change (e.g. pc1min <- warpRefMesh(species_1_mesh_pc1min, mesh.coord=land[,,1], ref = mshape, color="grey"). Is this an acceptable way to do what I want to do or is it recommended I do it another way?

Thanks,
Nick

messages.author: 511e44c7d1e1bab0
messages.subject: Re: [geomorph-r-package] warpRefMesh question
parts:
Nick,

if you do the PCA using plotTangentSpace you automatically get the predicted shapes at the extremes of each of the PCA axes in the $pc.shapes component of the output. This is not the same as plotting the specimen that exhibits the minimum value for e.g. PC1, as it only includes the predicted shape change across that specific axis. I think that would be a better way to go if you are interested in interpreting shape variation captured by each PC.

Cheers,

Antigoni
